Afternoon Translation

COMMUNISM

Sin Han Pao

LETTER FROM TID PIANG (徐炳根), FORMER MEMBER OF THE
CENTRAL COMMITTEE OF THE COMMUNIST PARTY, TO THE MEMBERS
OF THE CHINESE COMMUNIST PARTY.

Dear comrades and workers throughout the country:
I was arrested on April 29, 1930, while I
was directing the strike of electricity workers and
passed two years in prison. Before explaining the
cause of my repentance, I shall give an account of my
work with the Communist Party in the past.
I was a worker in the Foo Yih (傅益) Cotton
Mill, Shanghai Western District, for several years. My
enrolment with the Communist Party was not an accident
because during the May 30 Movement I was leading the
strike for racial revolution and for the benefit of the
workers. I was dismissed following the failure of
the movement. Later my wife died owing to unemployment.
I was not downhearted and I severed my relations with my
family and embarked on the revolutionary road as called
by the Communist Party. From 1925 up to the time of
my arrest, I had been always in the front line and on no
occasion did I desert the masses. At the time of my
arrest, I was a reserve member of the bogus Central
Political Bureau.
I have now finally discovered the treachery
of the murderous and cruel Communist Party. From the
time of the Kiangsu problem down to the struggles of the
anti-Li San Route, the anti-Third Plenary Session and
the anti-Fourth Plenary Session, the "Central" of the
Communist Party, under the control of the butcher Chen
Tou Seu and of Zung Shao Hgech (陳紹禹) and Zung Peung
Shien (秦邦憲), has often resorted to assassination and

January 13, 1933.
Afternoon Translation

COMMUNISM

comrades of the Fourth Plenary Session, Zung Shao Ngeoh,
Tsang en Tien (張聞天), Zung Paung Shien and others
resorted to betrayal of members to the authorities and
this led to the death of Ho Kzung Yoong (何孟雄) and 26
others. They used pistols to maintain order at meetings
of the Fourth Plenary Session; they mobilized the entire
body of the Special Administration Corps of the bogus
"Central" to deal with those comrades whose views did not
correspond with theirs. All these are facts and are not
fabrications. Was not their policy more cruel than that
of Li Lih San?
Comrades, I point out to you a recent case
of which you all must have had personal knowledge. Some
time ago a meeting of over 100 persons was held in the Kung
'oo Theatre (共舞台), Western District, at which 84
persons were arrested by the Police. These 84 persons
were mostly student comrades and members of the working
staff. At present the Communist Party is in a mess
and many members of the executive staff have deserted the
Party. This is because the doctrine of Lenin, Marx,
etc. is unsuitable to conditions in China. Zung Shao
Ngeoh and other running dogs are simply the tools of the
Third Internationale and by means of deceit they are
sacrificing the interests of the toiling farmers and workers
I now fully realize that the Communist Party cannot work for
the benefit of China; they are furthermore betraying the
interests of the workers. A labour strike, if it is
started by the masses themselves, may have a successful
conclusion, but if it is directed by the Communist Party,
it will end in failure because the desiderata of the Communist
Party are too impossible of attainment. The Communist Party
is not our friend but our enemy.
In the past I was used by the Communist Party
to carry out much work for the benefit of farmers and
workers. I have now fully come to my senses and wish
to offer my body and soul in the struggle for the race and
nation. I am determined to work for the Chinese Revolution
under the leadership of Central of the Chinese Kuomintang
Party.
Comrades, I hope that you will calmly study my
words and examine your past experiences. I know that your
livelihood at present is worse than what it was before.
Your condition is the same as that of the wharf coolies,
and your contractors, Zung Shao Ngeoh and others, are still
oppressing you. If you make a mistake, they will dismiss
you or send you to your death. I hope you will awake and
cease working as coolies for the Chinese Communist Party.
